## FAQ

### What is the Investing.com Earnings Calendar?

The Earnings Calendar is a free tool that tracks earnings report dates for publicly traded companies worldwide. It displays EPS and Revenue forecasts alongside actual results once released, so you can compare analyst expectations with reported outcomes in a single view.

### What is an earnings surprise? [...] The Earnings Calendar informs traders of quarterly and annual corporate earnings results versus expectations in real time. By default, earnings are listed in order of release date. Each earnings release includes the company’s ticker symbol, full name and the period for which the company is expected to release its earnings. The consensus forecast for each company’s EPS is listed alongside the prior period’s value. When the actual figure is released, it appears under the ‘Actual’ heading, in real [...] Most publicly traded companies report earnings four times a year, once per fiscal quarter. Earnings season typically begins a few weeks after each quarter ends, with the busiest reporting periods falling in January, April, July, and October. Not all companies report on the same date, so the Earnings Calendar helps you track which companies are reporting on any given day.
